claims.text: An actively learned moment tensor potential trained on sparse ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations from solid and liquid phases can accurately predict fusion free-energy differences.
The AL-MTP can faithfully reproduce vibrational entropy in both solid and liquid phases.
The AL-MTP can faithfully reproduce anharmonic entropy contributions to fusion.
The AL-MTP can faithfully reproduce electron–vibration coupling in both phases.
The proposed workflow will cost roughly ten times less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow will be faster than TOR-TILD.
Active learning will permit training on a small, carefully selected set of ab initio configurations from both phases.
The trained potential will be used with thermodynamic integration or another enhanced-sampling method to compute fusion free energies.
Learning the ab initio potential-energy surface will reproduce the thermodynamic properties controlling fusion.
Enhanced sampling with the learned potential will provide free energies with fidelity comparable to full ab initio molecular dynamics at substantially lower cost.
Moment tensor potentials encode local atomic environments.
Encoding local atomic environments ensures faithful reproduction of vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration effects.
The method is applicable to elemental and binary metals in a narrow temperature window around melting.
The method can extend to moderately complex high-entropy alloys near their melting points.
Performance in very highly multicomponent systems remains unvalidated and may be limited by electron–vibration coupling and extreme anharmonicity.
Explicit first-principles workflows have high computational demands for multicomponent alloys.
CoCrFeNi-based alloys can exhibit fcc and bcc phase structures.
Fusion free energies and entropy contributions will fall within experimental error margins.

A deviation greater than 10% from ab initio molecular-dynamics free energies, failure to reproduce key entropy contributions, or failure to reduce cost relative to TOR-TILD will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes elemental and binary systems but gives CoCrFeNi, a four-component alloy, as its example.

The hypothesis and mediator state that electron–vibration coupling is faithfully captured, whereas the uncertainty field says the potential may be unable to capture it fully in multicomponent systems included within the proposed scope.
